comments.body: The new fallback `content = Buffer.from(file.content, "utf8")` corrupts callers that pass a binary string, which is the documented contract. The docs at packages/core/core-flows/src/file/steps/upload-files.ts:25-27 and 51 say images use a binary string, and packages/core/types/src/file/service.ts:33 says the same. Any binary string with a byte above 0x7F fails the base64 round-trip check on line 63, so it reaches this branch. Each char 0x80-0xFF is then UTF-8 encoded into two bytes, so a JPEG or PNG written through uploadFilesStep (or the pattern at packages/modules/providers/file-s3/integration-tests/__tests__/services.spec.ts:41) is stored with damaged bytes. Before this change the same input went through `Buffer.from(content, "binary")` and was correct. The same heuristic also misreads plain text: a 4-character ASCII string such as "test" is valid canonical base64, so line 64 decodes it to 3 bytes (b5 eb 2d) and writes those instead of the text.

Same defect as local-file.ts:66. The fallback `content = Buffer.from(file.content, "utf8")` re-encodes a binary-string upload as UTF-8, so every byte above 0x7F is doubled and the object is stored corrupted. Binary-string callers are the documented contract (packages/core/core-flows/src/file/steps/upload-files.ts:25-27 and 51, packages/core/types/src/file/service.ts:33). Line 127 can also decode a short ASCII text such as "test" as base64 and write different bytes. Before this change, `Buffer.from(file.content, "binary")` handled these inputs correctly.
